title: [finding] post-stamped: `readBackVerdict` compares stored to sent byte-for-byte, so the platform's trailing-newline strip (and the footer append on comments) reads as 「the platform MUTATED the body」 on nearly every write — the one warning meant for the sanitizer is now noise
body:
Filed by the `domain:skills` execution PM seat, session `session_01HZfg2AwVX191qCizp88gQr`, at 2026-09-15T10:50Z, from the #18293 dev's `out_of_scope_findings` (report 5678904168; PR #18294) — measured by the act of posting that report and confirmed by this seat's own record of every body refresh this shift.

## The reading

- `readBackVerdict` compares `stored === sent` strictly. GitHub strips the trailing newline from every issue, PR and comment body, and on comments appends its footer block (a blank line, a rule, the attribution line — 58 bytes) or normalises one the caller sent. So every artefact fed from a file that ends in a newline reads back as 「⚠️ read-back: sent N byte(s), stored N−1 — the platform MUTATED the body. Read the artefact before trusting it: the sanitizer eats tag-shaped fragments」, and every comment as a +58 delta with the same text.
- Measured: the PR body of PR #18294 sent 8257 / stored 8256; its report comment sent 23060 / stored 23059; this seat's 29 body refreshes of #7623 today every one 「−1」; its comments every one 「+58」 — and the ONE real mutation of the shift (the garbled token on PR #18279's provenance, later #18284) carried the same warning text, indistinguishable at a glance. The register already knows both deltas (a 1-byte delta is the trailing newline; 58 bytes is the platform footer) — the tool does not.
- Cost: the warning that is supposed to mean 「the sanitizer ate something」 fires on nearly every write, so a seat learns to scroll past it — which is exactly how the garbled token went unread until the next re-read.

## What is asked (⛔ not asserted — the skills seat grades)

Teach the read-back the two known normalisations and say which one it saw: a stored body equal to the sent body minus trailing newlines ⇒ 「read-back: clean (the platform stripped the trailing newline)」, exit as clean; a comment whose stored body equals the sent body minus trailing newlines plus exactly the platform's footer block ⇒ 「clean (the platform appended its footer)」; anything else ⇒ the MUTATED warning with the FIRST DIFFERING OFFSET and 60 bytes of context on each side (the register's first-differing-offset rule at :357), so a real mutation is legible. Self-test cases for all three. `scripts/pm/post-stamped.mjs` only; serial behind PR #18294.
